answer.text: The spring parade in Ana's city and the harvest fair in Tom's town are quite different, but both are lively. The parade is far more crowded than the fair: thousands of people come to see the colourful costumes and listen to loud music. The parade is also noticeably older; it is about two hundred years old, whereas the fair is only fifty. In both places, families tend to spend the day together and share food. answer.text: Mia opened the kitchen door slowly. It creaked, and a faint scent of burnt toast filled the room. The kitchen was dim and damp, and somebody had left a cup of tea on the table. It was still warm. 'Who was here?' Mia whispered, and a shiver ran down her back. She had heard footsteps in the garden earlier, but she had told nobody. Then she noticed that the window was open. 'Grandma?' she called. 'It is only me,' a voice muttered from the dark corner. Grandma was sitting in her old chair, and she had not slept for two nights.
accepted: Mia opened the kitchen door slowly. It creaked, and a faint scent of burnt toast filled the room. The kitchen was dim and damp, and somebody had left a cup of tea on the table. It was still warm. 'Who was here?' Mia whispered, and a shiver ran down her back. She had heard footsteps in the garden earlier, but she had told nobody. Then she noticed that the window was open. 'Grandma?' she called. 'It is only me,' a voice muttered from the dark corner. Grandma was sitting in her old chair, and she had not slept for two nights.

Mia entered her grandmother's kitchen at midnight. The floor creaked, and a faint smell of coffee hung in the air. The room was dim, and someone had left the back door open. 'Who is there?' Mia whispered. Nobody answered. She glanced at the table: a cup of tea was still warm, so somebody had been there minutes before. 'Come out,' she snapped, although her hands were cold. Then a shiver ran down her back, because she had heard the same footsteps the night before. Finally a voice muttered, 'Do not shout, it is only me.' Grandma had come down for a glass of water.

When Mia opened the door, it creaked loudly. The kitchen was dim, and a faint scent of smoke filled the air. Someone had left a cup of tea on the table, and it was still warm. 'Is anybody here?' Mia whispered. Nothing moved. She glanced at the window, which was open, and a shiver ran down her back. She had locked it before dinner, she was sure. 'Stop hiding,' she snapped. Then Grandma appeared at the door and muttered that she had only wanted some fresh air.

answer.text:
Hi Carlos,

I am writing to give you an update on the volunteer guide. So far, I have completed three of the five sections, and the project is on track overall, although we are slightly behind on the last two sections.

The main obstacle has been a delay in the photos from the school. Without them, I cannot finish the sections about the garden and the library, and I have not been able to start the layout. I have already written to the school twice, but nobody has replied yet.

Meanwhile, I will be writing the two remaining sections, so they are ready as soon as the photos arrive. Next week I will also be testing the guide with two volunteers, and I will be collecting their comments. I will send you a short summary of their feedback on Friday.

I would be grateful if you could contact the school and ask them to send the photos by Wednesday. With your support, I am sure we can still finish on time.

Thank you very much for your help.

Best wishes,
Sara

prompt.es: Escribe la transcripción de tu charla de dos minutos (unas 170–210 palabras).

answer.text:
Have you ever tried to sleep while the traffic never stops outside your window? Today I will outline two ideas about noise in our city: why it is growing, and what we can do about it.

Firstly, let me explain why it is growing. Here is one statistic that surprised me: the number of cars in our city has doubled in ten years. Every new car adds more noise to our streets, and the noise does not stop at night. Moreover, the impact on our health is bigger than most people think. Noise makes us tired and nervous, and it makes it hard to concentrate at school or at work.

Secondly, what can we do? We can walk or cycle to school, we can ask the council for quiet zones, and we can talk to our neighbours about the problem. Who will make our city quieter if we do not? The council? The police? Or you and me?

To wrap up, let me recap my two ideas. The noise is growing because of traffic, and it harms our health. My takeaway is simple: small changes can make a quiet city. Thank you for listening, and I am happy to take your questions.

answer.text:
Have you ever walked past a dirty park and thought: somebody should do something? Today I will outline two ideas: the problem and a simple solution, a monthly cleaning day run by students.

Firstly, let me show you the problem. Here is one statistic that surprised me: every week, our school throws away more than two hundred kilos of paper. Last year, the park near our school was dirty for months, and nobody cleaned it. Think about the cost too: all the paper that we throw away is money that we could spend on new books.

Secondly, what can we do? I propose one Saturday a month, four groups of volunteers and two hours of work. Some people say that nobody will come, but other schools already do the same, and it works. Moreover, the impact would be bigger than the work itself: students would learn to take responsibility, and our neighbours would see that young people care. Yesterday the park was dirty; today we can make it clean. Who will do it if we do not? The council? The teachers? Or you and me?

To wrap up, let me recap my two ideas: the problem is real, and the solution is simple. My takeaway is this: a clean park begins with one Saturday. Thank you for listening, and I am happy to take your questions.

origin.audio: Tom's sister invited him to a party on Saturday. He thanked her warmly and said, I'd love to, but I might have other plans. When she asked what plans, he answered, Oh, nothing I can really talk about yet. Then he quickly changed the subject to her new flat.

origin.audio: At the family lunch, my aunt looked around the table and sighed, Some people only come when there is free food. Everyone went quiet, because we all knew that she was talking about my cousin, who had not visited for months. My mother quickly offered everyone more rice to change the subject, and my cousin, who had just arrived, smiled and said, I'm here for the company, but the rice does look lovely.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada réplica con su mensaje implícito.

feedback.es: Cada réplica esconde una petición, una queja o un reproche; la última es la respuesta diplomática que los esquiva con cariño.

origin.audio: On this week's podcast, an adviser reviews a company newsletter. She points out that the editor wrote that sales rose in three departments but never mentioned the other two. The figures do not prove that those teams struggled, she says, yet what was left out is revealing. A reader who jumps to conclusions may blame the managers, whereas a careful reader simply notes what the newsletter does not say and asks to see the numbers.

origin.audio: At the hearing, the police officer summarised the case. The muddy footprints pointed to the garden, and the broken window suggested that someone had broken in from outside. However, the receipt found in the suspect's coat cast doubt on his claim that he had spent the evening at his sister's house, since it showed that he had bought fuel near the school at eight o'clock. Even so, she insisted that the evidence was only circumstantial, and that a witness would have to corroborate it before anyone could be charged.

answer.text: The bakery on our street has been closed for five days, and I have noticed three clues. First, there is a delivery van at the door. Second, the front wall has been freshly painted. Third, somebody saw the owner with a new sign yesterday. Taken together, these clues suggest that the bakery is having a renovation, which seems the most plausible explanation. accepted: The bakery on our street has been closed for five days, and I have noticed three clues. First, there is a delivery van at the door. Second, the front wall has been freshly painted. The alternative that it is closing permanently is unlikely, so I can rule it out: nobody orders a new sign and paints the wall before leaving. Apparently, the owner plans to reopen soon. On balance, it would be unwise to speculate; I will ask him tomorrow to be sure.

answer.text: The trophy is missing from the cabinet, and I have two possible explanations. First, a stranger might have taken it during the night. Second, the cleaner could have moved it. Both ideas are possible at first, but only one of them fits the evidence. The door was locked all night, so a stranger can't have come in. In addition, the cabinet is not broken, which points to someone with a key. The cleaner has a key, came yesterday and has no alibi for Friday evening. On balance, the cleaner must have moved the trophy, although I can't be completely sure. The theory is plausible, but it would be unfair to accuse anyone yet, so we should ask the cleaner first.
accepted: The trophy is missing from the cabinet, and I have two possible explanations. First, a stranger might have taken it during the night. Second, the cleaner could have moved it. We have two possible explanations for the missing trophy. A stranger may have taken it, or the cleaner might have moved it. A stranger cannot have taken it, because the door was locked all night and the cabinet is not broken, so whoever opened it probably had a key. The cleaner has a key, worked yesterday and has no alibi for Friday evening. Since nothing else accounts for all the evidence, the most likely explanation is that the cleaner moved the trophy, perhaps to polish it. I am not certain, however, and it would be wrong to accuse her without proof. To be sure, we should ask the cleaner tomorrow and check who else holds a key.

prompt.es: Completa: «Te aconsejaría que descansaras unos días, aunque decides tú.»

feedback.es: I'd suggest that… es una recomendación amable que, en boca de un médico, equivale a una instrucción.

origin.text: I'd ___ that you rest for a few days, although of course the decision is yours. It might help your results.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Puede que el paciente necesite una segunda prueba.»

answer.text: The patient might need a second test

feedback.es: Might + verbo base suaviza la necesidad: en una consulta suele significar que conviene hacerla.

choices.text: That the doctor cancels the second test he has suggested.
That the doctor stops softening the news and speaks clearly.
That the doctor sends him the results of the first test.

feedback.es: El paciente ha leído los atenuadores y pide un mensaje claro: quiere saber si debe preocuparse de verdad.

origin.text: Dear Dr Lane, thank you for your message. I understand that the results are slightly unusual and that you would suggest another test. I would be grateful if you could tell me clearly whether I should be worried.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige el mensaje real del médico.

choices.text: The result is bad, and there is nothing more to be done.
The result is fine, and the medicine is only to be safe.
The result is bad, treatment is needed, and it can be managed.

feedback.es: No the best y I'm afraid anuncian mala noticia; la oferta del lunes y «we can manage» indican que hay tratamiento.

origin.audio: To be honest, the result is not the best, and I'm afraid we need to start the medicine soon. I wonder if you could come in on Monday, so that we can explain how to take it. It is important, but it is something we can manage.

prompt.es: Completa: «Su presión parece estar algo baja, así que la enfermera la revisará otra vez.»

feedback.es: Seems to be + adjetivo presenta la noticia con distancia y es un atenuador típico de la consulta.

That the answer was warm enough to make him change his plan.
That the answer was kind but also perfectly clear.

origin.audio: My friend Leo asked me to join his new business. I liked him and the idea, so I did not want to let him down. I said: It's a great idea, and I'm grateful that you asked me. Honestly, though, I'm a bit worried about the money, and I'm afraid I can't say yes this year. Perhaps we could start with a small project instead, and I'll take a rain check on the full business. Leo was not angry at all; he said he preferred a clear answer to a vague one.

prompt.es: Completa: «Me preocupa un poco el dinero este mes.»

feedback.es: A bit worried es un atenuador: muestra preocupación real sin dramatizar.

origin.text: Thanks for the invitation, but I'm afraid I must say no. Honestly, I'm a bit ___ about the money this month.

choices.text: That he likes the idea, but the rent makes him refuse.
That he dislikes the proposal and wants to end the idea.
That he is very happy and will sign the contract next week.

feedback.es: La respuesta alaba la idea y usa «rather more than I can manage» como atenuación de un rechazo real por el precio.

origin.text: Leo proposes to Tom that they move to a bigger flat in June. Tom replies: That sounds exciting, and I would love to live closer to you. Honestly, though, the rent is rather more than I can manage at the moment.

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿con qué propósito dice la hablante «I'll take a rain check»?

To keep the plan open for another day.
To cancel the plan for ever without saying so.

feedback.es: Take a rain check deja la puerta abierta: no cancela el plan, lo aplaza para otra ocasión.

origin.audio: It's a lovely plan, but I'm afraid I'm busy on Friday. Honestly, I've been working late all week, and I'd rather rest. Could we go on Sunday instead? If that doesn't work, I'll take a rain check.

prompt.es: Completa: «No quiero decepcionarte, así que seré sincera.»

feedback.es: Let someone down significa decepcionar o fallar a alguien; por eso se dice que no con sinceridad.

origin.text: I don't want to let you ___, so let me be honest: I'm afraid I can't join the project this year.

answer.text: Hi Mia, thank you for the invitation. It's a great idea, and I can see why you like it. Honestly, I'm a bit worried about this month: I have exams, and my time is very tight. I'm afraid I can't say yes to a film club every Friday, because I wouldn't be a good host and I don't want to let you down. Perhaps it would be better to wait until the exams are over. How about a film evening once a month instead? We could watch a film at your place next Saturday and then decide together. I'd rather do something small for now, and I would love to take a rain check on the weekly club. I hope you understand! See you soon, Ana

I'm afraid I can't say yes to a film club every Friday, because I wouldn't be a good host and I don't want to let you down. Perhaps it would be better to wait until the exams are over. Hello Mia, thanks for thinking of me. A film club is a nice idea. To be honest, I'm a little tired this month, and the exams are very close. I'm afraid I can't join every Friday, because I need that time to study. Maybe we could start in June, when my exams are finished. What if we watch one film together this Saturday instead? feedback.es: El mensaje eficaz reconoce la idea, rechaza con claridad, suaviza con tres atenuadores y termina con una alternativa concreta.

origin.text: Tu amiga Mia propone organizar un club de cine todos los viernes en tu casa. Tienes exámenes y poco tiempo este mes. To show Sara that he is irritated by her request.

feedback.es: La oferta de llevarla a la estación no cambia el no: lo hace más amable al dar una alternativa útil.

origin.text: I'm afraid I can't lend you the car for a whole month, Sara. I need it for work, and honestly, I'd feel worried if something happened to it. I could drive you to the station on Saturdays instead, if that helps.

She accepts the dinner, but asks to bring her sister.

origin.audio: Thanks so much for the invitation, Tom, it really means a lot. I would love to come to your birthday dinner, but I'm afraid I have promised to help my sister this weekend. Honestly, I'm a bit sorry about it. Could I take you out for a coffee on Monday instead?

prompt.es: Completa: «Prefiero quedarme en casa esta noche, si no te importa.»

feedback.es: I'd rather + verbo base expresa una preferencia suave y cortés.

origin.audio: Leo had been chosen to speak on behalf of the tenants, and he was nervous. At the meeting he told the landlord: Two people asked me to bring up something. Tom wanted to know whether the heating could be repaired before Friday, and Mia wondered why the rent had gone up again this year. The landlord looked at him for a moment and said that he would reply to both questions in writing by Monday. Leo thanked him and sat down, happy that he had got the message across without sounding angry.

prompt.es: Completa: «Tom se preguntaba si podría pagar el alquiler con una semana de retraso.»

feedback.es: Las preguntas de sí o no transmitidas con wondered se introducen con whether o if.

origin.audio: I understand your concern, and I wonder if we could find a solution together. The repair will start on Thursday, but I'm afraid the rent cannot change this year.

prompt.es: Escribe el mensaje a la casera: transmite las dos preguntas y responde con tacto.

answer.text: Dear Sara, thank you for your message. I understand that some tenants have paid the rent late, and I wonder if we could find a simple solution together. Honestly, I think the start of the month is a bit difficult for some people. On behalf of the flat, I would like to pass on two questions. Tom asked whether you could repair the heating before Friday, because it seems to be getting colder. Mia wanted to know why the rent had gone up this year. I'm afraid I can't answer that myself, so I would be grateful for your reply. Perhaps we could agree on one payment date each month instead, and everybody would know what to expect. I hope this is fine for you, and I would like to thank you in advance for your help. Best wishes, Leo
accepted: Dear Sara, thank you for your message. I understand that some tenants have paid the rent late, and I wonder if we could find a simple solution together. Honestly, I think the start of the month is a bit difficult for some people. On behalf of the flat, I would like to pass on two questions. Tom asked whether you could repair the heating before Friday, because it seems to be getting colder. Mia wanted to know why the rent had gone up this year. I'm afraid I can't answer that myself, so I would be grateful for your reply. Perhaps we could agree on one payment date each month instead, and everybody would know what to expect. I hope this is fine for you, and I would like to thank you in advance for your help. Best wishes, Leo

Hello Sara, thank you for writing. I'm sorry that some rent has arrived late, and I wonder if a fixed date could help everyone. It might be a bit hard for people to pay on the first day. I have two questions from my flatmates. Tom wondered whether the heating could be repaired before Friday, since it seems to be getting colder every night. Mia asked why the rent had gone up this year, and she would like to hear your reply. I'd suggest that we talk about both points on Saturday, if that is convenient. What if we agree on a fixed date each month instead? Thank you for your patience, and I hope we can find a fair answer. Kind regards, Leo

She added that time was running out before the board meets, and that she did not want to hear about another problem unless it came with a bright idea. Then she smiled and thanked us for our patience.

choices.text: She is angry and holds the whole team responsible for it.
She is under pressure, but she still appreciates the team.
She is relaxed and believes the deadline can move.

feedback.es: El silencio inicial y las imágenes muestran presión, pero termina sonriendo y agradeciendo la paciencia: valora al equipo.

origin.audio: At Monday's meeting, our manager opened with a long silence. prompt.es: ¿Qué postura defiende la autora sobre las metáforas cotidianas?

choices.text: They are quick, but a literal description is clearer.
They are easy to use, but they show a lack of effort.
They are useful tools for expressing feeling quickly.

feedback.es: La autora contradice a los críticos: en dos palabras la metáfora comunica lo que una descripción literal tardaría un párrafo en decir.

origin.text: Critics often say that everyday metaphors are lazy. I disagree. When a colleague tells me she feels down, she conveys in two words what a literal description of her mood would need a whole paragraph to explain, and everybody understands her at once.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito escribe la directora este correo a los equipos?

choices.text: To encourage the teams and collect ideas without adding pressure.
To warn the teams that they must work late until Friday.
To announce that the teams will receive fewer requests.

origin.text: Dear all, I know the last weeks have been a jungle, and a flood of requests has left many of you feeling down. I am not asking anyone to work late. I simply want each team to send me one bright idea by Friday, however small, so that we can decide before time runs out.

prompt.es: Completa: «El estudio era una selva durante la última semana del proyecto.»

feedback.es: Jungle es la metáfora del caos donde cada uno compite por hacerse oír (también se acepta zoo); no es una descripción de plantas.

origin.text: Everyone agreed that the studio was a ___ during the last week of the project: phones rang all day, every team wanted the same small space, and only the loudest people were heard.

choices.text: That the project will continue without any change at all.
That his departure will be a real loss for the team.

origin.audio: When Tom left the company, his manager called him the heart of the team. She said the office would feel cold without him, and that his bright ideas had kept the project alive for years. Tom smiled, but he admitted that he felt heavy as he packed his things.

prompt.es: Describe un mercado lluvioso con metáfora, símil, personificación y explicación.

answer.text: On a rainy Saturday the market was a grey river. People moved between the stalls like leaves on the water, and the rain danced on the roofs and whispered to the fruit. The lamps were golden apples in the dark morning, and the whole place seemed to breathe warm air. I chose the river because it shows how the crowd never stops moving, even when the weather is bad. The sellers called their prices, and the smell of bread and coffee made everybody smile. A hint of sadness hung over the umbrellas, yet the noise was so cheerful that I forgot the cold. It was a noisy, colourful place, and I felt small in the middle of it, like a boat on the river.
accepted: On a rainy Saturday the market was a grey river. People moved between the stalls like leaves on the water, and the rain danced on the roofs and whispered to the fruit. The lamps were golden apples in the dark morning, and the whole place seemed to breathe warm air. I chose the river because it shows how the crowd never stops moving, even when the weather is bad. The sellers called their prices, and the smell of bread and coffee made everybody smile. A hint of sadness hung over the umbrellas, yet the noise was so cheerful that I forgot the cold. It was a noisy, colourful place, and I felt small in the middle of it, like a boat on the river.

Yesterday the market was a big kitchen on a rainy day. The sellers shouted like cooks, and the crowd moved as slowly as a river between the stalls. The rain danced on the umbrellas and sang a quiet song. The fruit looked like small lamps, red and yellow and green, and the smell of bread and coffee was a warm hug for everybody. I chose the kitchen because it shows how warm and busy the place was, even when the sky was grey. Everybody was wet, but everybody was smiling, and the market kept breathing until the evening. A hint of sugar and smoke stayed in my clothes when I finally walked home, and I did not mind at all.

prompt.es: Escribe un ensayo con una metáfora extendida sobre aprender un idioma.

answer.text: Learning English is a long journey. At the beginning I was standing at the door with no map, and I felt lost. Grammar became my map, and vocabulary became my compass. Every class was a step, and every mistake was a wrong turn that showed me a new direction. Sometimes the road was long and I walked slowly, but I never stopped. Now I can understand songs, films and conversations, and I am not afraid of wrong turns any more. I still stay on course because I practise every day, even when I am tired, and my friends walk beside me and help me laugh at every wrong turn. Looking back, the journey taught me that patience matters more than speed. One day I will reach my destination, but the road itself is already a good place to live.
accepted: Learning English is a long journey. At the beginning I was standing at the door with no map, and I felt lost. Grammar became my map, and vocabulary became my compass. Every class was a step, and every mistake was a wrong turn that showed me a new direction. Sometimes the road was long and I walked slowly, but I never stopped. Now I can understand songs, films and conversations, and I am not afraid of wrong turns any more. I still stay on course because I practise every day, even when I am tired, and my friends walk beside me and help me laugh at every wrong turn. Looking back, the journey taught me that patience matters more than speed. One day I will reach my destination, but the road itself is already a good place to live.

Learning English is a garden. On the first day I planted a few words, and every morning I watered them with a little practice. Some words grew quickly and others needed more time, but I never stopped planting. Grammar was the ground, and my mistakes were the bad plants that I took out one by one. My teacher was a patient gardener, and my friends were the sun. Sometimes it was hard, and I felt lost in the garden, but I stayed on course by returning every day. Looking back, the garden taught me that patience matters more than speed. Today I have a few flowers, and I am happy, but I will keep planting new words every day. In the end, the flowers did not come quickly, but they came, and I am proud of every single one of them.

feedback.es: Un buen ensayo abre con la metáfora, la desarrolla con elementos del mismo campo, incluye una dificultad y cierra con una reflexión literal.

prompt.es: Escribe la escena de recuerdo que se pide en el recuadro.

answer.text: I remember standing on my grandmother's porch on hot summer evenings, when the air was warm and heavy and the scent of fresh bread drifted out of the kitchen. I can still hear the creak of the old gate and the echo of my cousins laughing in the garden. I will never forget watching the sun go down behind the hills while she told us stories about her own childhood. One evening I forgot to say goodbye when my parents took me home, and I still regret not hugging her that night. When I look back on those summers, I realise how much they shaped me. Now I must remember to call her every Sunday, because the scent of bread alone is not enough to keep a voice alive. Some memories linger for ever, small and golden, exactly as they were.
accepted: I remember standing on my grandmother's porch on hot summer evenings, when the air was warm and heavy and the scent of fresh bread drifted out of the kitchen. I can still hear the creak of the old gate and the echo of my cousins laughing in the garden. I will never forget watching the sun go down behind the hills while she told us stories about her own childhood. One evening I forgot to say goodbye when my parents took me home, and I still regret not hugging her that night. When I look back on those summers, I realise how much they shaped me. Now I must remember to call her every Sunday, because the scent of bread alone is not enough to keep a voice alive. Some memories linger for ever, small and golden, exactly as they were.

I remember playing in my grandfather's garden every summer, long before I understood how rare those days were. The air was warm, and the scent of ripe apples was everywhere. I can still hear the creak of the wooden gate and the echo of his voice calling us in for dinner. I will never forget eating under the big tree while he told funny stories about his youth. I regret not asking him more questions about his life, and I must remember to visit his house again this year. When I look back on those evenings, I realise that the smallest details are the ones that stay with me. Even now, when I close my eyes, that garden comes back, small and green and full of light. It is a vivid memory, and I do not want to forget it.

answer.text: Thank you, chair. My position is clear: the city centre should be closed to cars at weekends. Granted, congestion is a real problem, and some shops fear that they will lose customers. Nonetheless, the evidence from other cities suggests that pedestrian streets bring more visitors, thereby helping shops rather than harming them. With respect, my opponent says that free buses would be a better solution, but that plan would cost too much and may not prove viable. Admittedly, a car-free centre involves a trade-off, yet on balance the benefits outweigh the costs. A scheme whereby residents keep access to their homes would protect the people who live here. Thank you, chair. I am against a full ban on cars in the centre, and I would like to explain why. To be fair, my opponent is right that congestion is a problem, and I would not deny that pedestrian streets are safer. answer.text: Many students believe that one long night of study is the best way to prepare for an exam, but research suggests that regular short sessions may be more effective. A survey of 200 college students found that those who studied for forty minutes every day scored ten percent higher than those who studied only before the exam. This appears to show that regular review helps students retain information, although the effect may depend on the subject. For example, languages seem to benefit more from daily practice than essay subjects do. It could be argued that students who study every day are simply more interested in their courses, so the results should be read with care. To a certain extent, a good schedule matters more than the number of hours. In the long run, a short session every day is likely to be a better habit than cramming, but more research is needed.
accepted: Many students believe that one long night of study is the best way to prepare for an exam, but research suggests that regular short sessions may be more effective. A survey of 200 college students found that those who studied for forty minutes every day scored ten percent higher than those who studied only before the exam. This appears to show that regular review helps students retain information, although the effect may depend on the subject. For example, languages seem to benefit more from daily practice than essay subjects do. It could be argued that students who study every day are simply more interested in their courses, so the results should be read with care. To a certain extent, a good schedule matters more than the number of hours. In the long run, a short session every day is likely to be a better habit than cramming, but more research is needed.

Some people think that listening to music while studying improves concentration. However, a study of 120 teenagers suggests that silence may be better for difficult tasks. The teenagers who worked in a quiet room scored eight percent higher on a reading test than those who listened to music. This seems to indicate that music can distract students, although it might help with simple tasks such as copying notes. It could be argued that some students are used to music and feel calmer with it, so the effect may depend on the person. Largely for this reason, the results should be read with care. Nevertheless, there is some evidence that a quiet schedule with short sessions is likely to work better for most students, but the sample was small and more research is needed before we can be sure of it.

answer.text: Good morning, everyone. Let me summarise our study. One hundred and fifty students kept a study diary for a month, and the students who reviewed their notes every day scored twelve percent higher in a final test than the others. The findings suggest that daily review may help students remember more, and this appears to hold for most subjects. Some of you may have an objection, so let me reply to one of them: a classmate asked whether these students were simply more interested in their studies to begin with. That is a fair point, and it is a limitation of the study, because we did not measure interest. To a certain extent, you may be right, and we cannot generalise our results to every student. Nevertheless, the difference was large, and it is likely to be valid for students of our age. More research is needed before we can be sure, and another team would need to replicate our findings. For now, I would suggest trying daily review for one month. Thank you for listening.
accepted: Good morning, everyone. Let me summarise our study. One hundred and fifty students kept a study diary for a month, and the students who reviewed their notes every day scored twelve percent higher in a final test than the others. The findings suggest that daily review may help students remember more, and this appears to hold for most subjects. Some of you may have an objection, so let me reply to one of them: a classmate asked whether these students were simply more interested in their studies to begin with. That is a fair point, and it is a limitation of the study, because we did not measure interest. To a certain extent, you may be right, and we cannot generalise our results to every student. Nevertheless, the difference was large, and it is likely to be valid for students of our age. More research is needed before we can be sure, and another team would need to replicate our findings. For now, I would suggest trying daily review for one month. Thank you for listening.

Hello, everyone. To summarise, 150 students wrote in a study diary every day for a month. After the month, the students who reviewed their notes daily scored twelve percent higher in the final test. The results suggest that regular review might improve memory, and it seems to work for most subjects. Someone has asked whether these students were already more interested in their studies. That is a good point, and I accept it as a limitation of the study. It could be argued that interested students simply study more. That said, the difference was large, and the findings still seem to show a clear effect, so I think the conclusion is likely to be valid, although we need more research before we are sure. Another team should replicate the study with students from different schools. For now, I would suggest that we all try daily review for one month, and then compare our scores. Thank you for your attention.

answer.text: Good morning, everyone. My topic today is our school book club, and I will cover three points: how it started, how it has grown and what we plan to do next. Firstly, let me explain how it started. Two years ago, only twelve students came to the first meeting, and we sat in the corridor because we had no room. Now let's move on to the second point: how the club has grown. As you can see in my chart, membership rose steadily, from twelve to thirty in two years. Roughly half of the members are first-year students, and just under a third are boys. Finally, I would like to turn to our plan. We would like to organise a reading night in June and invite two other schools. To sum up, the club started small, grew gradually and is ready for a new challenge. The message I want you to take home is simple: a few friends and a corridor were enough. Thank you for listening. I am happy to answer any questions.

As you can see in my chart, my weekly distance rose gradually, from roughly five to around twenty kilometres in one year. I also take a short pause between exercises, and I keep a steady pace. Now I'd like to turn to my goal for next year. I hope to run a half marathon in the spring, and my friends will run with me. To sum up, running is cheap, simple and good for the head as well as for the body. Thank you very much for listening. Are there any questions?

answer.text: It was raining when I reached the deserted station, and my bag was heavy. I had promised Sara that I would be there at eight, but the last train had already left. A man was sleeping on a bench, and a small clock was showing the wrong time above the ticket office. I felt cold and afraid. What I remember most is the silence, which was like a wall between me and the rest of the city. I took out my phone, but it had no power. Then I heard a voice behind me. It was my old teacher who was standing there with an umbrella! She had seen me from the bus and had followed me inside. She laughed, gave me her phone and said, “Call Sara. She has probably been waiting for you.” I called, and Sara answered at once. She was not angry. In fact, she had missed the train too, and she was waiting at the next station. We met her an hour later, and we laughed about the whole night. I will never forget how kind both of them were.
accepted: It was raining when I reached the deserted station, and my bag was heavy. I had promised Sara that I would be there at eight, but the last train had already left. What I remember most is the silence, which was like a wall between me and the rest of the city. I took out my phone, but it had no power. Then I heard a voice behind me. It was my old teacher who was standing there with an umbrella! She had seen me from the bus and had followed me inside. She laughed, gave me her phone and said, “Call Sara. She has probably been waiting for you.” I called, and Sara answered at once. She was not angry. In fact, she had missed the train too, and she was waiting at the next station. We met her an hour later, and we laughed about the whole night. I will never forget how kind both of them were.

It was getting dark when I arrived at the cinema, and a long line was waiting outside. I had bought the tickets two days before, but when I looked in my bag, I understood that I had left them at home. My heart was beating like a drum. What I felt most was shame, because Leo had already told everyone that the film was his idea. I walked to the desk and explained the problem. The woman smiled and said, “Do not worry. Show me the message on your phone.” I looked for it, but my hands were shaking. Finally I found it. It was a small miracle that the message was still there! She checked the name, printed two new tickets and wished us a good film. When I found Leo, the film had already started, so we sat in the dark and whispered like children. Afterwards we walked home and he laughed at me all the way. I remember that night as the day I learned to check my bag twice.

Even so, I am convinced that the money would be well spent. Cheaper travel would help students, workers and older people who cannot afford a car, and it may also reduce traffic in the centre. Some say that buses would become crowded, and I agree that the service would need more vehicles. Perhaps the city could add a few routes at busy hours and review the plan after twelve months. It seems to me that nobody can be certain of the result before trying. However, doing nothing is also a choice, and it has costs of its own: noise, pollution and long delays. To sum up, free transport is a fair and sensible idea, and on balance I think it is worth a try.

Hello Sam, thanks for telling me how you feel. Your message suggests that I am not doing enough, and I can see why you are upset. Admittedly, I have not cleaned much lately, and I am sorry about that. Still, my new job means that I work late most evenings, so perhaps the real problem is time, not effort. I am not sure that a strict rule would help, but a simple calendar might. What if we share the tasks by day, and I take the bathroom and the kitchen at weekends? origin.audio: At the party, I told Ana that I had walked across the Andes in twenty days. She did not just say, how nice. She said, twenty days? On foot? Did you carry everything yourself? Then she leaned towards me and asked what had been the hardest night. Her voice went up at the surprising parts, and she kept nodding. By the end I had told her about the storm, the guide's broken radio and the dog that followed us for three days.

pairs: Wow! And how did you start?

origin.text: Leo spent five minutes describing his new project. His colleague replied, without looking up: 'That's interesting. Hmm. Sounds like a lot of work.' Then she asked him nothing and went back to her screen.

The first colleague was offended and decided to avoid her from then on.

feedback.es: La pausa, la mirada al celular y el «interesting» sin preguntas indican cortesía; por eso la primera colega deja el tema.

origin.audio: Two colleagues meet in the lift. One says, I've just got three new cats. The other pauses, says, oh, nice, and looks at her phone. Right, she adds, that's interesting. She asks nothing about the cats. Well, this is my floor. The first colleague says, lovely to chat, but she decides not to mention the cats again.

Her pause before answering and the glance at her phone.
The mention of the three cats and her saying «nice» at once.

feedback.es: La duda inicial y la mirada al celular son las pistas de desinterés; la llegada del ascensor, el «lovely to chat» y las gatas no prueban nada, y un «nice» suelto tampoco.

origin.text: My new team always says 'Interesting!' when I share an idea, but nobody ever follows up. Is that a polite way of saying no, or is it simply how they speak? Last week my manager nodded for ten minutes and then said she would think about it. I honestly cannot read her at all.

To ask the traveller to move quickly to the main point.

origin.audio: At dinner I sat next to a man who asked how much my flat cost, whether I was married and what I earned, all within five minutes. Each time I answered briefly, he moved on to something more personal. Then a woman on my other side said, you grew up in Cuenca? What was that like? I talked about the river for ten minutes without noticing the time. Only later did I understand the difference between prying and showing interest.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es fácil divagar durante minutos sobre tus propias noticias.»

feedback.es: Ramble on es seguir hablando sin un punto claro; la solución son turnos cortos y una pregunta final.

answer.text: In those days, my grandmother and I would bake bread every Sunday morning. She never used a recipe, and the whole house smelled of warm bread until noon. Gradually, I noticed that she was forgetting the steps, but she laughed it off, and I did not want to ask any questions. Meanwhile, I was busy with school and my friends. One Sunday, she did not come out of her room. I waited in the kitchen, and my hands were cold. Then I saw her sitting on the bed, pale and confused. 'I do not remember the recipe,' she whispered. Eventually, I sat beside her, and we wrote the steps down together. Since that day, I have read the recipe aloud every Sunday. Looking back, I think that quiet morning taught me that love can also mean remembering for someone else.

In those days, every Sunday my grandmother and I would make bread together, and she always said that she did not need a book. Little by little, I noticed that she was forgetting the order of the steps. At the same time, I was too busy with my friends to ask her about it. Then, one Sunday, the kitchen was silent. I found her sitting at the table, pale and confused, looking at the flour as if she had never seen it. Finally, I took her hand, and we wrote the recipe on a piece of paper. Since then, I have read it aloud to her every Sunday. Looking back, I realise that I was the one who learned the most that day.

origin.audio: When I was twelve, I lost my little brother at a street festival. For ten terrible minutes, I searched every stall, asking everyone if they had seen a boy in a green jacket. The music seemed to get louder, and my legs felt heavy. Then I heard him laughing. He was sitting on a box beside a street musician, wearing a paper hat twice his size. From that day on, I never let go of his hand in a crowd, and even now, at thirty, I sometimes reach for it.

origin.audio: My aunt tells the same story at every wedding. When she was twenty, she got on the wrong bus in Quito and ended up three hours away, in a village with no hotel. It was raining, and her only money was a ten-dollar note. A woman let her sleep above the bakery in exchange for help with the morning bread. She stayed a week, then a year, and then for the rest of her life: the woman's son is now my uncle. She always ends with the same line: nobody plans the best things in life.

answer.text: Thirty years ago, my father arrived in Madrid with one suitcase and a single phone number. At the airport, someone took his bag by mistake, and he left with a stranger's suitcase. Inside there were no clothes at all, only an old guitar. He had no money, so he played in the street to pay for his first room. One evening, the owner of a small restaurant stopped to listen and offered him a job. Was he scared? Terribly, but the music kept his hands busy. Did he ever find his suitcase? Never, and he says that he does not miss it. The takeaway? Sometimes the wrong suitcase is the right luck. Today he still plays in that restaurant, and the story has come full circle, because it began with a stranger and a bag.

Never, and he says that he does not miss it. The takeaway? Sometimes the wrong suitcase is the right luck. Forty years ago my father left home with one small suitcase and the address of a cousin in Madrid. At the airport, another passenger picked up his bag by mistake, so my father went home with a stranger's suitcase. When he opened it, there were no clothes inside, only an old guitar. He had no money, so he played in the street to pay his rent. One night, the owner of a restaurant heard him and gave him a job. Were you scared, Dad? Of course I was afraid, he told me, but playing calmed me down. Did you ever find your suitcase? Never, and I never missed it. Here is the lesson: sometimes a mistake turns out to be your luck. Today he still plays in that restaurant, exactly where the story began.

feedback.es: La historia tiene gancho, conflicto (la maleta cambiada), resolución (el trabajo en el restaurante), respuestas a las dos preguntas del oyente e idea final.

origin.text: Datos: tu padre llegó a Madrid hace treinta años con una maleta y un solo número de teléfono; en el aeropuerto alguien se llevó su maleta por error y él salió con otra que solo tenía una guitarra vieja; tocó en la calle para pagar su primera habitación; el dueño de un restaurante le ofreció trabajo. Un oyente pregunta: «Was he scared?» y «Did he ever find his suitcase?». Responde a ambas dentro del texto y cierra con una idea final.

feedback.es: Some form of compensation es la colocación para reparar el daño causado con dinero o una ventaja.

origin.text: We know the delivery fell short of what you expected, so we are prepared to offer some form of ___ for the delay.

prompt.es: Escribe la respuesta breve de la empresa a la reclamación de Carlos.

answer.text: Dear Mr Ruiz, thank you for your message, and please accept our apologies for the inconvenience. We will send a replacement oven by Friday, and we will offer you compensation for the delay, which fell short of the standard we aim for. Please contact us if you need any further assistance. Kind regards, Customer Service

feedback.es: La respuesta agradece, se disculpa, da una solución con plazo y cierra con cortesía en el mismo registro formal.

origin.text: Responde como la empresa: agradece el mensaje, pide disculpas, ofrece un horno nuevo antes del viernes y una compensación, y cierra con un saludo formal.

prompt.es: Lee la intervención de Ana en el acta. ¿Qué función cumple?

choices.text: She opens the session and explains how the evening will run.
She proposes a motion and asks the members to decide on it today.
She interrupts a speaker to correct something said earlier.

feedback.es: Ana saluda, presenta el orden del día y asigna el acta: abre la sesión, tarea propia de quien preside. No propone ni interrumpe.

hint.es: Piensa en qué hace quien preside al comenzar, antes de que nadie haya hablado.

origin.text: Ana: Good evening, everyone. Before we begin, let me remind you that we have three items on the agenda tonight and that Sara will write the minutes. Let's start with the new bench.

prompt.es: Completa: «Leo, creo que te estás saliendo del tema de este punto.»

feedback.es: Digress from es la colocación para apartarse del tema principal: lo que hace Leo al contar sus vacaciones.

hint.es: Es el verbo que significa salirse del tema; tras to va la forma base.

origin.text: Leo has been describing his summer holiday for ten minutes now. Ana smiles and says, «Leo, I think you are starting to ___ from the item we are discussing.»

prompt.es: Ordena: «Cada miembro debe esperar a la presidencia antes de tomar la palabra.»

answer.text: Each member must wait for the chair before they take the floor

feedback.es: Take the floor es la colocación de empezar a hablar con permiso; must wait for the chair marca la obligación de esperar.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hizo la presidencia cuando un miembro se fue por las ramas.

choices.text: She suggested a separate motion about the parking fines.
She brought the discussion back to the item in hand.
She asked the secretary to read the minutes aloud again.

feedback.es: La presidencia reconduce el debate al punto que tocaba («steered the discussion back»). Las multas de estacionamiento quedan fuera del tema.

origin.audio: At last night's residents' meeting, the chair opened the session by thanking everyone for coming and reading out the three items on the agenda. The secretary, who was writing the minutes, reminded the members that anyone wishing to take the floor should raise a hand first. Halfway through the first item, one member went off the subject and began talking about parking fines, so the chair politely steered the discussion back. A second member then proposed a motion about the bench, and, once it had been seconded, the chair asked everyone to vote.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué ocurrió justo antes de la votación.

choices.text: The secretary read out last month's minutes.
The chair announced the end of the meeting.
Somebody backed the motion about the bench.

feedback.es: La moción sobre el banco fue secundada («had been seconded») y solo entonces se votó; el acta y el cierre no se mencionan en ese momento.

Mia: The council does. Leo: That is a fair point, but we are drifting; the water is a separate item. Ana: Thank you, Leo. Let us return to Mia's proposal and ask the members to decide.

prompt.es: En ese acta, ¿qué da a entender Leo con su comentario sobre el agua?

choices.text: That the council should not pay for the garden water.
That the water question belongs under another item.
That Mia should drop her proposal about Saturdays.

feedback.es: Leo admite que la pregunta es razonable, pero dice que es «a separate item»: pertenece a otro punto. Ana lo confirma al volver a la propuesta de Mia.

choices.text: To end the meeting because it has already run over time.
To postpone the decision on the motion until next month.

feedback.es: La presidencia pide a Mia que concluya y da paso a Tom sin reprocharle nada: gestiona el tiempo con cortesía. Ni cierra la reunión ni aplaza la moción.

origin.audio: Right, that is the first item finished. Before we move on, may I remind everyone that we are already ten minutes over time? Mia, you have held the floor for quite a while, and Tom has been waiting patiently to speak. So, Mia, if you could wrap up in one sentence, Tom can ask his question, and after that we will put the motion to the members.

prompt.es: Completa: «Si nadie quiere añadir nada, pediré que se vote la propuesta.»

feedback.es: Call for a vote es la colocación fija para pedir que se someta algo a votación; ask for a vote también es posible, pero call for es la fórmula propia de quien preside.

origin.text: After a long and careful debate, the members agreed that the proposal was clear. The chair looked around the room and said, «If nobody wishes to add anything, I will ___ for a vote on the proposal.»

prompt.es: Según el acta, ¿qué deja claro la presidencia en su respuesta a Carlos?

choices.text: That his objection came too late to change the result.
That the vote must be repeated because of his objection.
That the secretary should remove the vote from the minutes.

feedback.es: Ana recuerda que las objeciones se plantean antes de votar: la decisión ya está tomada y se mantiene. No pide repetir la votación ni borrarla del acta.

origin.text: Minutes, item 4. Sara proposed moving the summer party to June. The members voted, and the proposal was approved. Carlos then objected that the hall would not be free that month. Ana, as chair, replied that objections must be raised before a vote, so the decision would stand.

origin.text: Carlos has suggested using the school hall on Fridays. Mia nods and says, «I would like to ___ on Carlos's idea and use the hall in summer too.»

prompt.es: Tom propone subir la cuota. ¿Qué respuesta expresa una reserva sin cerrar el acuerdo?

choices.text: I see the need, so I have no objection to raising it at all.
I see the need, but I have my doubts about raising it so sharply.
I see the need, but I am simply not willing to discuss it at all.

origin.text: Tom: I suggest we raise the yearly fee to thirty dollars, because the roof needs repairs and the club has no savings.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué pidió Leo para suavizar la subida de la cuota.

choices.text: A payment plan paid over several months.
A delay until the roof repairs are finished.
A lower fee for members under eighteen.

feedback.es: Leo pide una cuota menor para menores de dieciocho. El plan de pagos es de Mia y la condición de las reparaciones, de Tom.

origin.audio: At the sports club's monthly meeting, the treasurer proposed raising the yearly fee to cover the cost of a new roof. Leo said he supported the idea in principle, but he was not sure that thirty dollars was realistic for students, and he asked whether the club could find a middle way with a lower fee for members under eighteen. Mia then offered to add to that suggestion with a payment plan, and Tom, who had opposed the fee at first, told the group that he could now go along with it, provided the roof repairs were finished before winter.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué condición pone Tom para aceptar la subida.

choices.text: That the repairs are completed before winter begins.
That students always pay less than other members.
That the treasurer shows the accounts once more.

feedback.es: Tom acepta «provided the roof repairs were finished before winter»: la condición es el calendario de las obras, no el precio para estudiantes.

origin.text: Hi all, thanks for circulating the proposal to move our meetings to Thursdays. In principle I have no objection, and I can go along with the change, although Thursdays are hard for me because of my evening class. I wonder whether we could find a middle way and switch between Tuesdays and Thursdays? Either way, I would rather have a decision by the end of the month. Best, Sara

choices.text: To announce that she will miss the Thursday meetings.
To complain that nobody consulted her about the proposal.
To explain the difficulty without refusing the change.

feedback.es: Sara da el motivo de su dificultad pero mantiene su aceptación y propone una solución intermedia; no anuncia que faltará ni se queja de que no la consultaran.

origin.text: Carlos: I propose we hold the tournament in July. Mia: I support that, and I think we could use it to raise money for new goals. Tom: I am not convinced that July works, because half the players will be on holiday.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué ha cambiado en la postura de la hablante.

choices.text: She has decided not to vote because the sides cannot agree.
She still rejects both options but will not say so openly.
She has moved from a likely no to backing a middle path.

feedback.es: Venía a votar en contra, pero ve que ambos piden algo razonable y propone un reparto de días: pasa de la oposición a apoyar una solución intermedia.

origin.audio: I will be honest: I came tonight fully planning to vote against this. But after hearing both sides, I can see that neither of you is asking for the impossible. So here is my suggestion: we keep Saturdays as the main day, which is what Leo wants, and Tom gets his Sunday sessions once a month. If nobody has a serious objection, I would be happy to go along with that.

prompt.es: Completa: «Me gusta en principio, pero dudo que sea viable con dos voluntarios.»

feedback.es: Feasible significa viable en la práctica; Sara acepta la idea pero cuestiona si se puede llevar a cabo con tan poca gente.

He rejects it, unless the signs are made much smaller.
He backs it, but only if the council funds the signs.

feedback.es: Carlos apoya el carril con una condición («only if»): que el municipio pague los carteles. Sin ella votaría en contra.

origin.text: Carlos: I am in favour of the bike lane, but only if the council agrees to pay for the new signs. Otherwise, I am afraid I would have to vote against it.

origin.audio: Last Thursday, the residents' association met to discuss turning Oak Street into a cycle route. Carlos argued strongly in favour, pointing out that two children had been hurt on that street last year. Mia accepted the risk but insisted that removing the parking would hurt the elderly residents, who depend on their cars. Leo suggested a compromise: a trial of three months, after which the association would review the results. Everybody accepted it, although Mia said she would wait for the results before changing her mind. Sara will write to the council by Friday.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué postura mantiene Mia al final de la reunión.

choices.text: She has dropped her objection now that a trial is planned.
She accepts the trial but has not changed her mind yet.
She rejects the trial and will keep opposing the route.

feedback.es: Mia acepta la prueba pero dice que esperará a ver los resultados antes de cambiar de opinión: su postura sigue siendo cautelosa; ni ha retirado su objeción ni rechaza la prueba.

origin.audio: The neighbourhood meeting was going well until Tom began a long story about a parking ticket he had received in March. After several minutes, Ana, who was chairing, cut in politely: if I could just come in here, Tom, I think we are drifting from the agenda. She suggested that he hold that thought until the end, when there would be time for other business. Tom nodded, a little embarrassed. Then Mia offered to paraphrase the council's letter, so that everybody would be sure of the deadline, and Ana thanked her and asked the secretary to note it down.

origin.text: Reunión de la asociación de vecinos sobre un mercado semanal. origin.audio: Sara had prepared carefully for her scholarship interview, but the first question took her by surprise: why did she want the place? She had a rehearsed answer about loving science, yet one panel member smiled and asked her to tell them about a moment when that love had actually changed something. Sara hesitated, then described how she had organised a recycling project at her school, what went wrong in the first month and how she fixed it. Afterwards, the panel asked what she would do if the school stopped supporting the project. She said she would look for a company to help and ask former students for advice.

She says the figures fit the claim, but they cannot show that the menu is the cause. She recommends a trial in a second school before anyone draws a conclusion.

feedback.es: Whereas une dos cláusulas completas que contrastan: subida en el centro, bajada en las afueras.

feedback.es: El informe solo muestra que las dos caídas coincidieron en julio; eso es una correlación, no una causa demostrada.

origin.text: From the clinic's report: 'Among the 400 members who joined the gym in January, 300 were still attending in June. Attendance at the gym and at the swimming pool both fell in July, when the gym closed for repairs for two weeks.'

origin.text: Reader's note: the headline says 'Bike lanes end traffic jams'. Yet the council's table, quoted lower down, shows that journey times on the main road fell from 34 to 31 minutes after the lanes opened, and that the road is still busy at eight.

origin.audio: In the meeting, the coordinator presented the school's sports figures. Overall, swimming rose from thirty-five to seventy-one members in three years, whereas running stayed at around eighty. One teacher said that the new pool had caused the rise. The coordinator answered carefully: the increase appears to be partly linked to the pool, but the fees also fell, so other reasons could matter too. She would not call it a cause. If the trend continues, she added, swimming is likely to overtake running, and in that case the pool may need longer opening hours.

The school may need to build a second pool if swimming keeps growing.

answer.text: Overall, the number of students who play tennis rose steadily from 35 in 2022 to 71 in 2025, so it has roughly doubled in three years. Compared with tennis, football hardly changed: around 80 students took part every year. Meanwhile, the difference between the two sports has narrowed from 45 students to only 12, although football remains the more popular sport. The biggest jump came in 2024, when 14 more students joined. This appears to be partly linked to the new indoor court, although the figures do not prove it. However, the school budget stayed the same, which suggests that other reasons also matter. If this trend continues, tennis is likely to overtake football by 2026; consequently, the school may need extra coaches. Of course, this is only an estimate.

origin.audio: At the end of her talk on the school reading club, Mia took two questions. A teacher asked whether the club would keep growing, and Mia thanked him for a fair question. Finally, she admitted one limitation: the data cover only three years.

To warn that the estimate of sixty members is certain to be wrong.

origin.audio: Thank you for sending your draft on student sleep. The structure is clear: you open with a summary and then state your aim. However, your method section is missing, so readers cannot tell how many students answered, or how the survey was carried out. Also, your findings section slips into opinion, with phrases like I think and sadly. A report should keep an impartial tone and save interpretation for the conclusion. Fix those two points, and the recommendation, which is already well written, will be much more convincing.

answer.text: The aim of this report is to describe how students travel to school. The method was a survey of 100 students carried out by the school council, and every answer was included in the analysis. The main findings show that 52 percent of respondents come by school bus, whereas only 6 percent cycle. The remaining students either walk, 30 percent, or come by car, 12 percent. Furthermore, 35 students said that the bus journey takes more than forty minutes. It appears that long journeys may be a problem for students who live far away, although more evidence is needed. The conclusion is that the school bus is the most common way to travel. Therefore, it is recommended that the school should consider a second morning bus, which would probably shorten the daily commute. The survey was somewhat limited, so the results should be treated as tentative.
accepted: The aim of this report is to describe how students travel to school. The method was a survey of 100 students carried out by the school council, and every answer was included in the analysis. The main findings show that 52 percent of respondents come by school bus, whereas only 6 percent cycle. The remaining students either walk, 30 percent, or come by car, 12 percent. Furthermore, 35 students said that the bus journey takes more than forty minutes. It appears that long journeys may be a problem for students who live far away, although more evidence is needed. The conclusion is that the school bus is the most common way to travel. Therefore, it is recommended that the school should consider a second morning bus, which would probably shorten the daily commute. The survey was somewhat limited, so the results should be treated as tentative.

This report gives an overview of how students get to school. A survey of 100 students was carried out by the school council. The findings show that more than half of the respondents, 52 percent, use the school bus, while 30 percent walk, 12 percent come by car and only 6 percent cycle. In addition, 35 students said that the journey by bus takes longer than forty minutes. There is some evidence that long journeys may affect students who live far away, but it remains unclear how many are affected. To conclude, the bus is the main way to travel. We recommend that the school consider an extra bus in the morning, which would shorten the daily commute for many families.

The aim of this report is to show how students travel to school. We surveyed 100 students, and every student answered in class, so all the replies could be included. According to the survey, 52 percent travel by school bus, 30 percent walk, 12 percent come by car and 6 percent cycle. Nevertheless, the bus is not always convenient: 35 students said that the journey takes over forty minutes. It seems that this may be a problem for those who live far away, although the survey cannot prove it. Therefore, we recommend a second morning bus. The conclusion is that the school bus is essential, and a second one could improve the daily commute for many students.

feedback.es: El mini informe lleva el objetivo, los resultados con cifras, una afirmación matizada, la conclusión y una recomendación, con tono neutro.

origin.text: Encuesta del consejo escolar a 100 estudiantes sobre cómo llegan al colegio: 52 en autobús escolar, 30 a pie, 12 en auto y 6 en bicicleta. El viaje en autobús dura más de 40 minutos para 35 estudiantes. Escribe unas 140 a 220 palabras: objetivo, método, resultados con cifras, una afirmación matizada, la conclusión y una recomendación, con tono neutro.

prompt.es: Lee el borrador y elige qué debería mejorar el resumen oral.

origin.audio: A student is comparing her written report with her oral summary. The report has a method section and a long list of findings. In the talk she will skip the method and mention only two findings, because the listeners cannot read the tables. She will repeat the key point at the end, so nobody forgets it.

prompt.es: Escribe el resumen oral de un minuto con anuncio, punto clave, cautela y recomendación.

answer.text: I will outline the main findings of our survey on digital habits. The key point is that 64 of the 80 students use a phone for more than three hours a day. Only a minority, 20 students, sleep fewer than seven hours. It appears that heavy users tend to sleep less, although more evidence is needed. To conclude, we recommend a phone-free hour before bed.
accepted: I will outline the main findings of our survey on digital habits. The key point is that 64 of the 80 students use a phone for more than three hours a day. Only a minority, 20 students, sleep fewer than seven hours. It appears that heavy users tend to sleep less, although more evidence is needed. To conclude, we recommend a phone-free hour before bed.

I will briefly present our survey on digital habits. The main point is that most students, 64 out of 80, use a phone for more than three hours daily. It seems that heavy users may sleep less, but we cannot be sure. Only 20 students sleep fewer than seven hours. In conclusion, we recommend one hour without phones before bed.

I will give an overview of our digital habits survey. The key finding is that 64 of our 80 students use a phone for over three hours a day. It appears that heavy users tend to sleep less, although more evidence is needed. In short, we recommend a phone-free hour before bed.

feedback.es: El resumen anuncia, da el punto clave con una cifra, añade una cautela y cierra con una recomendación, en frases cortas.

prompt.es: Lee el parte: ¿qué da por casi seguro el pronóstico?

origin.text: Coastal forecast: a storm will definitely reach the harbour this evening, although the wind might drop a little before the last ferry leaves. Fog is unlikely, and there is only a slim chance of clear skies tomorrow morning.

feedback.es: «All but certain» es lo más seguro de la escala: la nieve en altura. La tormenta es solo una posibilidad real y el corte de luz no se descarta.

origin.audio: On this morning's radio show, the forecaster was careful with her wording. She told listeners that snow on the high ground was all but certain, that rain in the valley was highly likely by the afternoon, and that a thunderstorm was still a distinct possibility after dark. Clear skies, she added, were unlikely before Sunday, and she would not rule out a short power cut in the mountain villages. Anyone planning a long drive north, she said, should decide by noon rather than hope for the best.

In the unlikely event that we have to evacuate the ship, please do not use the lifts: walk calmly to the nearest exit and wait for instructions from the crew.

Conditions are likely to deteriorate quickly in the afternoon, and anyone still on the high ground by two should take shelter rather than try to continue. Treat this as a serious alert.

prompt.es: Escribe seis avisos de seguridad para una ruta de montaña.

answer.text: Safety notices for the ridge walk. 1. Do not start the climb unless the sky is clear at seven in the morning, because the route becomes hazardous when the rocks are wet. 2. You may walk along the ridge provided that the wind is light, and you may stop at the shelter as long as you leave no rubbish. 3. Take a torch and a spare battery in case you come down after dark. 4. Carry a waterproof jacket in case the afternoon storm arrives earlier than the forecast says. 5. You had better turn back if the path is icy, because a fall here is a real danger and help is hours away. 6. When in doubt, err on the side of caution: it is sensible to rest in the shelter and wait for the guide. Take precautions, and enjoy the walk.

Notice 1: Nobody should go up unless a guide has checked the path that morning, because the rocks can be very slippery. Notice 2: The shelter is open to everyone provided that you leave it clean and tidy. Notice 3: Bring a warm coat and a torch in case the night is cold or you finish late. Notice 4: You had better start early if you want to reach the summit before the clouds arrive. Notice 5: It is safe to cross the bridge as long as it is dry, but if you are not sure, err on the side of caution and use the lower path. Notice 6: Keep your phone charged in case you need help, and take precautions against the wind, since it can change very quickly on the ridge.

The second hazard is the long descent: tiredness is the root cause of most falls, so we stop for ten minutes every hour and nobody walks at the back alone.

answer.text: Good morning, everyone. This briefing has three parts: the hazards, the risks and the preventive measures we take. The first hazard is ice on the ridge. It is likely after such a cold night, and the consequence could be a serious injury. To prevent a fall, all participants must check their equipment, and you had better walk slowly. The second hazard is the river. In the unlikely event that the water rises, we will turn back at once. There is a slim chance of thunderstorms after two o'clock, so we will be off the ridge by one. Nobody should cross the river unless the guide says it is safe. Please carry a torch in case we come down after dark. If something goes wrong, we will look for the root cause, not for someone to blame. Are there any questions?

Hello, team. Today I want to explain two risks. The main hazard is the wind on the high ground. Strong gusts are highly likely, and the consequence could be a fall or another serious injury. To prevent it, we will stay on the marked route, and you had better hold your hats. The other hazard is the cold. The odds are that it will freeze tonight, so everybody must bring a warm coat, provided that there is space in the bag. In case anyone feels dizzy, tell me at once. Unless the forecast improves, we will not climb the summit, and in hindsight that will be the right choice. Does everyone understand the plan?

answer.text: Rule 1: Dogs must be kept on a lead, except in the fenced area, in order to protect children and other animals, given that some dogs are not used to crowds. Rule 2: Music may be played on condition that it does not disturb other visitors, because the park is a quiet place for many families, and loud music is to be switched off at nine in the evening. Rule 3: Bicycles are to be left at the racks, apart from delivery bikes and children's bikes, so as to keep the main path clear for people on foot. The committee will review all three rules after six months, since a fair rule should change when the park changes. Anyone who disagrees may write to the committee, and please read these rules carefully before you enter.

First, rubbish must be taken home, except on festival days, because the bins are full by noon and the park looks dirty for the next visitors. Second, fires may only be lit in the marked area, given that dry grass burns easily and a single spark could close the whole park for a week. Third, dogs are to be kept on a lead, apart from guide dogs, in order to keep the playground safe for small children, who are often afraid of big animals. Finally, the gates shall be locked at ten unless the committee has approved an event, since neighbours need quiet at night. These rules are fair, because each one has a reason.

origin.text: Dear neighbours, we are writing to explain why plots will no longer be handed down within a family. origin.audio: Ms Ortiz, from the garden committee, explained the new policy. Our rationale is simple, she said: plots should be shared fairly. The waiting list is long, so each family will be limited to one plot. origin.audio: Hi Tom, it's Sara. I have thought about your offer, and I like the idea of a two-year contract. However, the rent you suggest is a little too low for me. Here is what I can do: I will waive the deposit on the understanding that you pay by the first of each month, and if you could look after the garden, we could settle at nine hundred and fifty. Let me know whether that package works for you before Friday.

choices.text: That she is open to a deal, but wants some changes.

feedback.es: Le gusta la idea del contrato de dos años, pero el alquiler es bajo y propone su propia versión: está abierta al trato con cambios.

origin.text: Thanks for your message. We could accept a shorter contract of one year on the understanding that the rent stays the same. If you could also waive the deposit, we could sign this week. In return, we are willing to pay the first three months in advance.

origin.audio: The tenant called the landlord to discuss next year's rent. The landlord said that, in principle, he could accept 900 dollars a month, subject to a two-year contract. The tenant replied that she could commit to two years only if the heating was repaired first. The landlord thought about it, then offered a solution: he would repair the heating in October, and she would sign in September. They agreed to meet halfway, but he warned that his agreement was provisional until his partner approved it.

origin.audio: Mia phoned Carlos to discuss her rental contract. Carlos began by saying that he could agree to 900 a month in principle, but that the figure was only tentative, because his partner had not seen it yet. Mia said she could commit to two years, if the heating was repaired before October. Carlos answered that he could not promise the repairs for October, only for the end of November. They finally agreed to meet halfway: the repairs would be done by the middle of November, and the contract would be signed only after that.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez. ¿Qué muestra el acuerdo final sobre la fecha de las reparaciones?

choices.text: That Carlos obtained exactly the date he had offered.
That both sides moved away from their first date.

feedback.es: Mia quería antes de octubre y Carlos a finales de noviembre: acuerdan mediados de noviembre, es decir, cada uno cede; no se mantiene ni la fecha de Carlos ni la de Mia.
